name: GRAND
full_name: Giant Radio Array for Neutrino Detection
summary: A staged international radio-array project seeks cosmogenic tau neutrinos by observing highly inclined air showers over very large areas. Implemented prototypes test the approach before a full observatory.
physics_targets: Radio detection of inclined air showers
detection_principle: Radio antennas on favourable terrain detect geomagnetic emission from air showers, including those from Earth-skimming tau leptons. Autonomous triggering and rejection of impulsive radio backgrounds are central challenges.

sites.name: GRAND@Auger
sites.location: Pierre Auger Observatory site near Malargüe

status.label: Multiple stages
status.evidence: Prototype arrays are implemented; the final global array and its neutrino exposure remain future goals.

timeline.event: Full science and design report released.
Antenna deployment began at Xiao Dushan, China.
Commissioning and calibration of a partial GP300 array reported.

collaboration.name: GRAND Collaboration
collaboration.participants_note: Institutions listed here are selected documented participants; the official collaboration page provides the complete membership.

key_parameters.name: Full GRAND concept
key_parameters.value: Up to 200,000 antennas over approximately 200,000 km²; long-term design

key_parameters.name: Documented deployment
key_parameters.value: ICRC2025 abstract reports 50 detection units at the Chinese site

results.summary: Measured radio backgrounds and calibration signals while developing self-triggered air-shower reconstruction. The complete GRAND sensitivity remains a design projection.

science_scope: Parameters refer to the named apparatus or explicitly identified design phase. Projections describe sensitivity goals and are not observations.

media.caption: Detection-principle diagram for GRAND10k from Figure 16 of the original GRAND design paper: a mountainside antenna array receives radio signals from cosmic-ray or Earth-skimming tau-neutrino-induced air showers.
